claims.statement: Insurance AI adoption and EIOPA governance expectations create a real assurance problem across claims and customer interaction use cases.

The compliance trigger is narrower than the original pitch: life and health pricing is expressly high-risk, while claims communications require use-case classification and sectoral governance rather than an automatic high-risk label.
An ongoing monitoring platform sold to insurers may face financial-sector ICT-provider diligence, security, access, audit, contractual, and exit requirements depending on function criticality.
The Polish insurer base is too small for an 80-insurer domestic scenario; material scale needs vendors, administrators, or Central European expansion.
Existing insurance governance deployments, horizontal continuous-testing tools, formal management-system certification, and a published insurance benchmark create strong substitutes and incumbents.

No reviewed source establishes lawful access to representative Polish claims outputs, procurement recognition of a new seal, local willingness to pay, renewal, expert cost, or conservative unit economics.

contrary_evidence: Poland had only 47 insurance companies at end-2025.
Credo has an insurance/reinsurance governance case and Giskard offers continuous evaluation with a free entry tier and sales-led enterprise tier.
ISO/IEC 42001 and formal conformity processes are stronger recognized assurance substitutes than a new private seal.
An insurance-domain LLM benchmark has already been published outside Poland.
Not every claims AI use case is high-risk under the AI Act.
